summary: Both occurrences already supply the existing I and III Infectum examples at 57/7 and 103/43; add no duplicate even though each cell has only one quotation.

Both I and III have an angry experiencer as grammatical subject and a target marked by ʕal. III maġḏ̣əb does not mean ‘make angry’ in this verse; preserve the entry's noncausative zornig werden gloss.
The I clause is a projected consequence with g-, while III occurs under dlo in an apprehensive clause. Neither supplies a new form box or a different lexical sense.
The Arabic etymology and unusual noncausative III are inherited lexical facts, not evidence of a light-verb collocation or a new Detransitive.
Is there a productive semantic or dialect distinction between I ġoḏ̣əb and III maġḏ̣əb beyond these two contexts? The supplied evidence only confirms their shared ʕal-target anger meaning.
